biography.plain_text: Alberto Roemmers was an Argentine pharmaceutical businessman who expanded the laboratory founded by his German immigrant father into one of Latin America's major drugmakers. Born in Buenos Aires, he studied business and biochemistry before leading the family enterprise. He also built a lasting involvement in competitive sailing alongside his sons.

long_biography.plain_text:
Alberto Roemmers favoured a small management structure that could make decisions quickly, a preference he passed on to his successor as chief executive. The pharmaceutical group combined that approach with local managers who knew their markets and could act without a rigid chain of command. The group kept research, manufacturing and marketing within its operations, alongside this decentralised management.

He also backed his eldest son's proposal to create IntraMed, an online service for medical communication and education. With his mother and sister, he established a foundation in his father's memory that supported health research and teaching. Its work included scientific meetings, nursing education and grants for investigators.
